decisions.reason: Underside service access does not change the separate rigidity and vibration-resistance requirements; the same message already records the tower-stability change.
Requiring serviceability underneath does not necessarily alter the accepted enclosure size or deep-well form.
The source does not change the raised platform's height, purpose, or edge-to-edge alignment; service access can coexist with the current platform requirement.
Underside maintenance access does not change the required clearance for 12-ounce cups beneath the spouts.
The service-access decision is unrelated to the raised-base logo's style, font, leaf treatment, or letter case.
Underside serviceability does not modify the spout's location, orientation, fabrication style, geometry, or pour direction.
The source decision does not affect machine placard text, placement, faces, or letter case.
Access beneath the machine for maintenance does not change the independently specified bowl-removal and swapping behavior.
The maintenance-access requirement does not replace or otherwise modify the current component-sourcing and custom-spout strategy.
Underside service access does not alter the selected bowl capacity, deep-well form, or capacity-selection priorities.
Serviceability underneath does not change the solenoid valve mechanism, button actuation, isolation behavior, or closed-state behavior.
The source decision concerns maintenance access and does not modify the required dispensing flow, froth preservation, sequence, or pour direction.
